drafts.title: Keep ride comfort comfortable on broken pavement
drafts.description: When driving on visibly broken or potholed roads, passengers experience a composed, non‑jarring ride — bumps feel absorbed and the car does not feel harsh or unsettling.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized 'broken pavement' test route driven at 30–60 mph, at least 75% of a representative sample of drivers and passengers rate ride comfort as 'comfortable' or better in a post-drive survey.
assumptions: Standardized test route and survey protocol are available for successor validation.
Adaptive or improved suspension tuning and tire choices are available for the successor generation.
uncertainties: Perception-based surveys can vary with user expectations and seat position.
Improvements may trade off with sporty handling preferences for a minority of customers.

drafts.title: Offer at-a-glance charger compatibility and routing that finds compatible fast chargers quickly
drafts.description: When planning or on a trip, the vehicle clearly shows which fast chargers are compatible and finds suitable stops quickly so drivers are not delayed or confused by incompatible plugs or payment requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Trip planner returns compatible high-power chargers for a requested route with compatibility details (connector, max power, payment) for ≥95% of public fast chargers along the route, and the UI displays results within 30 seconds for typical 200-mile trips.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date charger network databases and roaming/payment integrations is available at launch.
Cellular connectivity is sufficient for live database queries on route planning.
uncertainties: Third-party charger data quality and availability vary by region and provider.
Some chargers may be temporarily offline or have inaccurate published metadata.

drafts.title: Make charge state visible from the outside at a glance
drafts.description: When plugged in, the charge port indicator clearly communicates charging status (charging, complete, error) so owners can tell state without unlocking or walking to the screen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: External charge-port indicator is readable in daylight from 3 meters and in low light; in a user test ≥95% of participants correctly identify charging, complete, and error states within 3 seconds.
assumptions: A color-coded or icon-based external indicator is permitted by regional lighting regulations.
Standardized user-test protocol for readability is available.
uncertainties: Ambient lighting and viewing angle may reduce visibility in certain parking situations.

drafts.title: Reduce distracting wind noise at highway speeds
drafts.description: At and above typical highway speeds, exterior wind noise is low and not distracting so drivers can hold conversations and enjoy media without raising volume.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a straight highway at 75 mph (≈120 km/h), measured interior A-weighted SPL from exterior wind sources at the driver's ear is ≤65 dB(A) and in a consumer panel test ≥80% of drivers do not rate wind noise as 'distracting'.
assumptions: Standardized measurement positions and test windows are used for SPL measurement.
Production glass seals, mirror design and door seals are production-intent.
uncertainties: Roof racks, aftermarket accessories, or open windows significantly change wind noise.
Driving posture and head position affect perceived noise.

drafts.title: Make lane keeping assist steering smooth and non‑jerky in curves
drafts.description: When lane keeping assist is active in marked curves, the system steers with smooth, predictable inputs so drivers do not experience abrupt or nervous corrections.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In on-road validation on marked curves (radius down to 150 m) with lane-keeping active and speeds 30–70 mph, ≥90% of test drivers rate steering corrections as 'smooth' or better in a blinded user evaluation.
assumptions: Validation protocol includes a representative set of curve radii and lane markings.
Production-level chassis and steering tuning used during tests.
uncertainties: Tuning that reduces nervousness may reduce maximum lane-hold precision in extreme conditions.
Driver preference for intervention aggressiveness varies between users.

drafts.title: Provide a real-world single-charge range target of 600 miles
drafts.description: For customers who prioritize long distance between charges, offer a vehicle configuration that achieves a real-world single-charge driving range in the 600‑mile class so longer trips require fewer stops.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Under a representative real-world driving profile (combined highway and mixed city) and EPA-equivalent testing, the vehicle achieves ≥600 miles (≥965 km) single-charge range in the advertised configuration.
assumptions: Achieving 600 miles requires next‑generation battery energy density (e.g., significant improvements vs current lithium-ion), major vehicle lightweighting and aerodynamics, or the use of a range-extender powertrain option.
Public charging infrastructure and customer charging habits remain comparable to today.
EPA-equivalent test cycles and claims verification are accepted for customer-facing range statements.
uncertainties: Real-world range depends heavily on driver behavior, payload, climate control use and ambient temperature.
Supply-chain and cell-technology availability at scale are uncertain within a 3–5 year horizon.

drafts.title: Request for Level 3 automated driving type approval in Germany (out of scope — regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the car obtains type approval for Level 3 automated driving in Germany.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for Level 3 homologation in Germany (regulatory/type-approval request).
assumptions: This draft documents a regulatory/type-approval wish; homologation and type-approval activities are governed by external regulators and corporate compliance teams.
uncertainties: Approval timelines depend entirely on regulatory frameworks and BMW's certification programs.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory/type-approval request — homologation is out of scope for product requirements.

drafts.title: Request that the powertrain complies with CARB emission limits in all US states (out of scope — regulatory requirement)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the vehicle's powertrain meets California Air Resources Board (CARB) emission limits across the US.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for CARB-compliant powertrain in all states (regulatory compliance request).
assumptions: Regulatory emission compliance is governed by homologation and engineering certification processes, not by product-facing experience specifications.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulatory compliance request — out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request for UN R155 cybersecurity approval (out of scope — regulatory requirement)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the vehicle fulfils UN R155 cybersecurity type approval.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for UN R155 cybersecurity type approval (regulatory request).
assumptions: Type approval and certification processes are handled by engineering and compliance teams; the customer-facing outcome (secure vehicle) can be specified separately if customers request explicit data controls.

drafts.title: Request that the battery complies with the EU battery passport regulation (out of scope — regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the battery follows the EU battery passport regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for battery passport compliance (regulatory request).
assumptions: Battery passport compliance is a regulatory/data-reporting activity outside direct customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Request for 800 V vehicle electrical architecture (out of scope — engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the car uses an 800 V electrical architecture.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for 800 V electrical architecture (engineering-level specification).
assumptions: Electrical architecture is an engineering specification; customer-facing outcomes (faster charging times) should be specified instead if desired.
uncertainties: Implementation affects component suppliers and vehicle architecture choices.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific technical architecture request — engineering specification out of scope.

drafts.title: Request for 22 kW onboard AC charger (out of scope — engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the onboard AC charger is upgraded to 22 kW.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for 22 kW onboard charger (component-level specification).
assumptions: Onboard charger power is an engineering detail; the customer-facing desire is faster AC charging which can be captured as a separate outcome if requested.
drafts.scope_reason: Component-level power rating request — out of scope.

drafts.title: Request for solid‑state battery cells with 400 Wh/kg (out of scope — engineering/materials specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the battery uses solid‑state cells with energy density ~400 Wh/kg.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for solid-state cells at 400 Wh/kg (materials/cell-technology request).
assumptions: Cell chemistry and energy-density targets are engineering and supply-chain issues; customer-facing outcomes (range, weight, safety) should be specified instead.
uncertainties: Commercial availability of such cells at scale within 3–5 years is uncertain.
drafts.scope_reason: Cell-technology/materials specification — out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for specific front brake disc diameter (395 mm) (out of scope — engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the front brake discs have a diameter of 395 mm.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for 395 mm front brake discs (component/dimension request).
assumptions: Brake disc diameter is an engineering/mechanical specification; customer-facing outcomes (braking feel, fade resistance) should be specified instead.

drafts.title: Request for a named lidar supplier for highway assist (out of scope — supplier preference)
drafts.description: Customers asked that highway assist uses a lidar sensor from a named supplier.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customer signal recorded: request for a specific lidar supplier (supplier-level preference).
assumptions: Supplier selection is a procurement decision; customer-facing outcomes are system performance and reliability which should be specified instead.
uncertainties: Supplier availability and contractual agreements affect feasibility.
drafts.scope_reason: Supplier- or component-choice request — out of scope for product-facing requirements.
